statement: Given a probability distribution $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$ with mean vector $\vec{\mu} = (\mu_1, \mu_2, \dots, \mu_N)^\mathsf{T}$ and positive semi-definite covariance matrix $\mathbf{\Sigma}$, the Mahalanobis distance of a point $\vec{x} = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_N)^\mathsf{T}$ from $Q$ is defined as $d_M(\vec{x}, Q) = \sqrt{(\vec{x} - \vec{\mu})^\mathsf{T} \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1} (\vec{x} - \vec{\mu})}$. Between two points $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in \mathbb{R}^N$ with respect to $Q$, it is defined as $d_M(\vec{x}, \vec{y}; Q) = \sqrt{(\vec{x} - \vec{y})^\mathsf{T} \mathbf{\Sigma}^{-1} (\vec{x} - \vec{y})}$.

symbols.meaning: observation or test point vector in Euclidean space
second point vector in Euclidean space
mean vector of the distribution Q
covariance matrix of the distribution Q
Mahalanobis distance from point x to distribution Q
Mahalanobis distance between points x and y with respect to distribution Q
factor matrix from decomposition \Sigma = S^T S (e.g., symmetric standard deviation matrix)

properties.why: The distance from a point to a distribution Q is equivalent to the two-point distance between the point and the mean vector \vec{\mu}
By the spectral theorem \Sigma can be factored as S^T S, showing Mahalanobis distance is Euclidean distance after a whitening transformation
Axes are rescaled to unit variance and whitened to be uncorrelated, taking into account data correlations

properties.property: For a normal distribution, Pr[\vec{x}] d\vec{x} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\det(2\pi \mathbf{\Sigma})}} \exp(-d^2 / 2) d\vec{x}
properties.why: The exponent of the multivariate normal probability density function is proportional to the negative squared Mahalanobis distance -d^2/2

properties.property: d^2 follows a chi-squared distribution with n degrees of freedom for an n-dimensional normal distribution
properties.why: Squared Mahalanobis distance represents the sum of squares of n independent standard normal variables after whitening

properties.property: Invariance under full-rank affine transformations of the affine span of samples
properties.why: Linear transformations and translations of coordinates are compensated for by the transformation of the covariance matrix
Relates the squared Mahalanobis distance directly to the regression leverage statistic h

assumptions.breaks_when: The affine span of the samples is not the entire R^N, causing \Sigma to be singular and non-invertible

assumptions.assumption: The distribution Q has well-defined, finite mean vector \vec{\mu} and covariance matrix \mathbf{\Sigma}
assumptions.breaks_when: The underlying distribution lacks finite first or second moments

failure_modes.signature: Matrix inverse \Sigma^{-1} does not exist or yields infinite/undefined values
failure_modes.cause: Sample size is smaller than the feature dimension, or features exhibit perfect multicollinearity, reducing the rank of the affine span

failure_modes.signature: Masking or swamping of outliers, or inflated distances for normal observations
failure_modes.cause: Sample mean and covariance matrix are sensitive to extreme values; non-robust estimators are pulled by outlier points
